devices.name: Metonymy
devices.definition: Naming something by a word closely associated with it — cause for effect, container for contents, author for writings.

devices.name: Ellipsis
devices.definition: A word or words deliberately left out, to be supplied by the reader — compression and force.

occurrences.note: " Beware that none touch the young man Absalom."
that " Ishbosheth " is the word to be supplied, as is done in italics
"The channels of the sea appeared."

devices.name: Synecdoche
devices.definition: Substituting a part for the whole, or the whole for a part (“all the world”; “flesh and blood”).

occurrences.note: " Now therefore the sword shall never (lit., not for ever) depart from thine house ": i.e., while David or his family lived
" In the sight of all Israel ": lit., for all Israel's eyes: i.e., for anybody to see that chose
" And Absalom... and all the men of Israel ": i.e., the greater part of Israel
Mephibosheth is called " the son of Saul." " Son " is here put (by Synecdoche) for his grandson
Mephibosheth said to David, " All of my father's house were but dead men before my lord the king": he means his father's father

devices.name: Anthropopatheia
devices.definition: Ascribing to God human feelings, parts, or actions, by way of condescension to us.

devices.name: Heterosis
devices.definition: Exchange of one grammatical form for another — of tense, number, person, degree, or mood (e.g. a future used for a command).

occurrences.note: " How hast thou known (i.e., how dost thou know) that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead ? "
" By the hand of my servant David to save my people Israel": i.e., I shall save
" And the king lamented over Abner, and said, Will Abner die as a fool dieth ? " (i.e., as in AV. Died Abner

devices.name: Rhetorical question
devices.definition: A question asked for effect, not for an answer — to affirm, deny, or provoke thought.

devices.name: Epanadiplosis
devices.definition: A clause encircled — beginning and ending with the same word.

devices.name: Idiom
devices.definition: A peculiar usage of the Hebrew or Greek that does not carry its literal force — an idiom to be rendered by its sense, not word for word.

occurrences.note: "A city and a mother": i.e., a metropolitan city

devices.name: Anadiplosis
devices.definition: The word ending one clause is repeated to begin the next, linking them.

devices.name: Paroemia (proverb)
devices.definition: A proverb — a wayside-saying in common use, cited or coined.

devices.name: Polyonymia
devices.definition: Heaping up several different names or titles for the same person or thing.

devices.name: Catachresis
devices.definition: One word used for another only remotely related — a deliberately incongruous transfer.

devices.name: Hyperbole
devices.definition: Deliberate exaggeration, not meant literally, that drives a point home vividly.

occurrences.note: Saul and Jonathan " swifter than eagles," " stronger than lions."

devices.name: Periphrasis
devices.definition: Circumlocution: a description put in place of the plain name of a thing.

occurrences.note: "That falleth on the sword": i.e., is put to death by the public executioner

devices.name: Polyptoton
devices.definition: Repetition of the same root word in different inflections (“dying you shall die”).

occurrences.note: "And David fasted," ///., fasted a fast: i.e., completely or truly fasted
" And all his servants wept very sore." In Hebrew the figure is " wept a great weeping greatly."

devices.name: Ampliatio
devices.definition: An old name kept for a person or thing after the reason for it has passed (“the blind man” once healed).

devices.name: Anaphora
devices.definition: The same word or phrase begins a run of successive clauses, hammering a theme.

devices.name: Antimetabole
devices.definition: Words repeated in reverse order and grammatical relation (“sabbath for man … man for sabbath”).

devices.name: Aposiopesis
devices.definition: A sentence broken off unfinished, as if the speaker cannot or will not go on.

devices.name: Epizeuxis
devices.definition: Immediate repetition of a word for intense emphasis, with nothing between (“Lord, Lord”).

devices.name: Euphemism
devices.definition: A softened or decent expression put for one that is harsh or delicate (“fallen asleep”).

devices.name: Hypallage
devices.definition: Interchange: a word logically belonging to one term is grammatically attached to another.

devices.name: Irony
devices.definition: Saying the opposite of what is meant, so the real sense is felt through the contrast.

occurrences.note: Michal to David: " How glorious was the king of Israel to-day ! " That this was hypocritical is shown by verse 16: " She despised him in her heart." And so David understood it (verses 21, 22). Note

devices.name: Parallelism
devices.definition: Successive lines echo one another in structure — saying the same thing twice, or balancing matched clauses.

devices.name: Paronomasia (wordplay)
devices.definition: A play on words that sound alike but differ in sense — pun, rhyme, near-repetition.

devices.name: Pleonasm
devices.definition: A deliberate redundancy — more words than strictly needed — to underline or solemnise.

devices.name: Polysyndeton
devices.definition: Conjunctions (“and … and …”) piled up to slow the pace and weight every item.

devices.name: Synonymia
devices.definition: Amassing synonyms — words of like meaning — to enforce and enlarge a point.
